title: Jesus wept (John 11:28–44)
hookLine: he weeps with Mary, then calls Lazarus out and says: unbind him
last: THOUGH HE WERE DEAD, YET SHALL HE LIVE.

lines: THE SAME WORDS, A SECOND SISTER.
cards: Martha goes home and whispers to her sister: the Master is here, and he's asking for you. Mary gets up quickly and goes out. The mourners follow her, thinking she's going to the tomb to weep there.

She finds Jesus, falls at his feet, and says exactly what her sister said: "Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died." Same sentence, different sister. But this time Jesus doesn't answer with a teaching.
No I am. No question. He looks at her, crying, and at the people crying with her.

teach.b: John says "he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled." The Greek word for groaned is strong, almost angry, a deep shudder. He asks where they've laid him.
Come and see, they say, the words Jesus once used to his first disciples, now leading him to a grave. And then: "Jesus wept." Two words in the King James Bible, and a whole verse.
He knows what he's about to do. He's just told Martha, I am the resurrection. And he weeps anyway.
John lets grief and faith stand side by side. The people watching say: "Behold how he loved him!" At the tomb, a cave with a stone across it, he says, take away the stone.
Martha, practical to the end, objects: "Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days."
Jesus prays aloud, then cries with a loud voice: "Lazarus, come forth." And the dead man comes out, still wrapped hand and foot in grave clothes, his face bound with a cloth.
Then the last command: "Loose him, and let him go."

teach.h: LOOSE HIM, AND LET HIM GO.
teach.b: Not Jesus. The people standing around. Jesus calls Lazarus to life; the community unwraps him.
This week we've walked a long way: Siloam, synagogue, the door, hireling, Hanukkah in winter, Martha on the road, and now tears at a tomb, and a man walking out of it.

how: Christians often turn to "Jesus wept" in times of grief, as a sign that mourning is not a failure of faith; the raising of Lazarus is read in some churches in Lent, and the Orthodox Church keeps Lazarus Saturday before Palm Sunday.

games.q: you're standing at the tomb. Jesus says: take away the stone. you're Martha. what do you say?
games.why: practical Martha warns him: four days dead. Jesus answers that she'll see the glory of God, and the stone is moved.

practice: Think of someone who has come through something hard, an illness, a loss, an addiction, a bad season, but is still wrapped in the old cloths: loneliness, shame, a debt or practical problem, other people's memories of who they were.
Ask what small part of that you could help loosen: a ride, a meal, an invitation, forgetting the old story. If you pray, hold them before God; if not, hold them in mind kindly.

wordCard.voice: Jesus wept. Two words in the King James Bible: Jesus weeping with Mary at his friend's grave, moments before calling him out.

orig.note: Greek: he shed tears. A quieter word than the loud wailing of the mourners around him.

carryVoice: Your line: loose him, let him go. Another week on the path, and a good one to end on.
